account: Mehmet Can Duran, a school bus driver in Tokat, Turkey, was fined 2,400 TL by an honorary traffic inspector (fahri trafik müfettişi). He allegedly let a student off outside the designated stop. Webtekno says that he had stopped at a pedestrian crossing to let people cross (Webtekno, 7 February 2025). Not wanting to pay a lawyer, he had an objection petition written by artificial intelligence. Webtekno identifies it as ChatGPT. Akşam's İHA report names no tool (Akşam, 6 February 2025). The petition stressed that the inspector had submitted no image or document supporting the fine. The Tokat Civil Court of Peace (Sulh Hukuk Mahkemesi) found for Duran and annulled the fine within three weeks (Akşam; Webtekno). The reports, published on 6 and 7 February 2025, do not give the dates of the fine or the ruling.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT, per Webtekno, drafted the objection that pointed to the absence of any image or document behind the fine. The court annulled the fine on that ground. The decisive fact was the inspector's missing evidence, which Duran could have pleaded himself. What the system contributed was a petition in legal form at no fee. Neither report quotes the petition or the ruling.
